Integration by Parts

Run the product rule backwards to trade one integral for another. The area splits into two pieces, each computed separately.

A hard integral becomes a boundary term plus an easier integral. In the area picture, one big rectangle splits into two pieces. Both computations agree to the last decimal.

For example, measuring a 🍰 cake's area gets easier when you swap to a full rectangle minus one piece. Split the measuring and even awkward shapes become manageable.

Examples & Exercises

Prove integration by parts completely: if u,vu, vu,v are C1C^1C1 on [a,b][a,b][a,b], then ∫abu dv=[uv]ab−∫abv du\int_a^b u\,dv = [uv]_a^b - \int_a^b v\,du∫ab​udv=[uv]ab​−∫ab​vdu.

Integrate the product rule (uv)′=u′v+uv′(uv)' = u'v + uv'(uv)′=u′v+uv′ and apply the fundamental theorem of calculus.

∫abu(x) v′(x) dx=[u(x) v(x)]ab−∫abv(x) u′(x) dx\int_a^b u(x)\,v'(x)\,dx = \bigl[u(x)\,v(x)\bigr]_a^b - \int_a^b v(x)\,u'(x)\,dx∫ab​u(x)v′(x)dx=[u(x)v(x)]ab​−∫ab​v(x)u′(x)dx
Show proof

  1. Since u,vu, vu,v are C1C^1C1, u′,v′u', v'u′,v′ are continuous, the product uvuvuv is C1C^1C1, and (uv)′=u′v+uv′(uv)' = u'v + uv'(uv)′=u′v+uv′ (the product rule). Each term u′vu'vu′v, uv′uv'uv′ is a product of continuous functions, hence continuous — so both are integrable on [a,b][a,b][a,b].

  2. Integrate (uv)′=u′v+uv′(uv)' = u'v + uv'(uv)′=u′v+uv′ over [a,b][a,b][a,b]: ∫ab(uv)′ dx=∫abu′v dx+∫abuv′ dx\int_a^b (uv)'\,dx = \int_a^b u'v\,dx + \int_a^b uv'\,dx∫ab​(uv)′dx=∫ab​u′vdx+∫ab​uv′dx. The FTC turns the left side into ∫ab(uv)′ dx=[uv]ab\int_a^b (uv)'\,dx = [uv]_a^b∫ab​(uv)′dx=[uv]ab​.

  3. Hence [uv]ab=∫abu′v dx+∫abuv′ dx[uv]_a^b = \int_a^b u'v\,dx + \int_a^b uv'\,dx[uv]ab​=∫ab​u′vdx+∫ab​uv′dx, and moving ∫abu′v dx\int_a^b u'v\,dx∫ab​u′vdx across gives ∫abuv′ dx=[uv]ab−∫abu′v dx\int_a^b uv'\,dx = [uv]_a^b - \int_a^b u'v\,dx∫ab​uv′dx=[uv]ab​−∫ab​u′vdx — i.e. ∫abu dv=[uv]ab−∫abv du\int_a^b u\,dv = [uv]_a^b - \int_a^b v\,du∫ab​udv=[uv]ab​−∫ab​vdu. Complete. (Tao Proposition 11.10.1.)
